purpose.description: Evaluate how observation delay affects target identifiability and determine the minimum temporal access required to restore factorization.
purpose.role: Extend Interface Theory from hidden-state ambiguity to delayed observation systems.
not_used_for: claiming all delayed systems are non-identifiable
replacing temporal interface design with faster sampling

system_class.description: Dynamical systems where observations are delayed relative to underlying state evolution.

observation_operator.definition: Returns observations offset by delay tau.

target.description: Future target dependent on system trajectory beyond observation time.

lag_results.failure_mode: irrecoverable collapse under tested interface budget

criterion.statement: target-relevant future directions must remain distinguishable after delay

failure_pattern.description: Increasing lag collapses distinct trajectories into identical delayed histories.

observed_transition.meaning: Beyond this point the tested interface family loses sufficient temporal access.

relationship.pattern: approximately linear cost increase with delay
relationship.interpretation: additional temporal information compensates for lost immediacy

successful_case.statement: Delay increases required interface refinement until observation fibers become target-pure.

failure_case.statement: When delayed observations merge target-divergent trajectories, factorization fails.

decision.meaning: Temporal delay is an interface resource constraint rather than an automatic impossibility condition.

notes: Delay converts accessible present information into a temporal inference problem.
The relevant quantity is not delay alone but whether delayed observation preserves target purity.
Additional history or interventions can compensate for lost temporal alignment.
